WORKLOG — travel_protection_desk / task 0  (kept up to date from Step 0 onward)

STEP 0 — DRAW, ASSET LEDGER, SCOPE CLAIM
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/tasks/travel_protection_desk --tasks 2 printed:
  {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4]}
Task 0 is therefore a tree of exactly three problems (root + 2 prerequisite problems) whose
computations carry 5, 4 and 4 declared factors. Assignment: the root settlement takes 5, the
supplier-recovery declaration 4, the outstanding loading charge 4.
Occupied before this task: nothing (this is the first task of the difficulty).
Claimed by this task: base subjects care_premium_charge, care_claim_recovery and care_claim_payout;
extended policies care_ext_outstanding_loading_charge, care_ext_supplier_recovery_declaration and
care_ext_settled_benefit_payment; task tools charge_destination_loading_6e26c317,
declare_supplier_compensation_6de86425 and settle_benefit_payment_411249ab.
Left for task 1: the whole declaration-and-rating side of the charter — care_insured_amend
(care_policy_amendment), care_premium_adjustment (the re-rating half of care_premium_rating) and
care_claim_file (care_claim_filing) — which is an independent, load-bearing tree of three problems
with its own root (a claim the customer files in person) and its own prerequisite chain. Nothing in
task 1's space is touched here: this task raises a premium CHARGE and never an adjustment, files no
claim, and amends no declared particular.

DESIGN THESIS
Surface goal the customer volunteers: "the insurer allowed my lost-luggage claim in June and nothing
has been paid." That points at one problem only — the settlement of an allowed claim.
The genuinely scored core parameter: paid_amount_usd on that settlement.
Between the goal and that number the policy puts two prerequisites the customer never mentions:
 (1) the certificate's premium lines must carry every rating component its declared particulars call
     for, and the destination loading for the asia_pacific region it declares was never posted;
 (2) the benefit the certificate records as consumed must carry a restoration for every amount a
     supplier has paid the traveller for a loss already settled under it, and the airline paid her
     600.00 in August against the very delay the certificate settled in May.
Depth: goal -> settlement -> (restoration -> the airline ledger) and (rating component -> the club
tier). Breadth: the settlement reads the decision ledger, the payout ledger, the recovery ledger, the
deductible ledger and the plan's tier parameters in parallel; the loading reads the premium ledger
and the club membership in another difficulty; the restoration reads the air ledger in another
difficulty and the claim ledger here.
Observable terminal state: one destination loading premium line, one recovery row, one payment row.

CHECK CARD 1 — BASE-INVARIANT CARD
subject care_premium_charge:
  care_premium_rating — no structured eligibility gate; its scope governs how a premium component is
    rated. Inherited item by item except the one clause declared in overwrite ("the destination
    loading is the plan's single percentage for the region declared"). The minimum-premium clause,
    the once-per-certificate policy fee clause and the "loadings are added and not compounded" clause
    are all untouched and still hold: this policy adds ONE loading line and compounds nothing.
  care_club_and_bundle_interaction — no structured eligibility gate. Inherited except the declared
    clause ("the club tier held on the issue date decides the discount applied to the premium"). Its
    other clauses stand: the discount acts on the rated premium and never on the policy fee, and a
    corporate programme rate and a club discount remain mutually exclusive (no corporate programme is
    on this certificate — care_policies.linked_air_booking_id points at an air booking whose
    corporate_program_id is empty).
subject care_claim_recovery:
  care_subrogation — no structured eligibility gate. Two clauses declared in overwrite; the rest
    stand, in particular "A recovery is applied against the payment it reverses and never against a
    different claim or a different policy" (the gold call passes source_claim_id = the travel-delay
    payment row) and "A plan on which subrogation does not apply makes no recovery at all"
    (TripGuard Plus carries subrogation_applies true).
subject care_claim_payout:
  care_claim_settlement — no structured eligibility gate. Two clauses declared in overwrite; the rest
    stand, in particular "Payment is made to the policyholder in the currency the premium was paid
    in" (USD on every premium line of this certificate).
  care_agg_benefit_coordination — no structured eligibility gate. Its coordination clauses do not
    bind here: the traveller holds one other protection certificate (WLC2907145) but it is closed,
    covers a 2024 European journey and answers no part of this incident, so no second policy answers
    the same loss and nothing is coordinated.
TIME GATES: the care charter carries exactly one time eligibility, care_free_look.inside_free_look,
and it applies_to care_cancel. None of this task's three subjects is care_cancel, so there is no time
gate to inherit and temporal_feasibility is [] — checked against the blueprint rather than assumed.

CHECK CARD 2 — BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
The narrowest object the request points at is the insurer's decision row on claim reference
BG-5520-26 standing against certificate WLC3318472 — initial_state.care_claims.be63fa2e-bc8a-49d6-9b53-fd83571aa24f. The
correlation key the settlement writes back is source_claim_id = that decision row; the claim
reference BG-5520-26 additionally ties the payment to the claim the customer read out.
Rows that enter the aggregates, and why they belong:
  - allowance: the decision rows on THIS certificate (97886242-e3e2-487f-9b17-505edc9c2c9c, be63fa2e-bc8a-49d6-9b53-fd83571aa24f); LATEST by decided_date
    picks be63fa2e-bc8a-49d6-9b53-fd83571aa24f (2026-06-18) over 97886242-e3e2-487f-9b17-505edc9c2c9c (2026-05-20).
  - benefit consumed: the payout row 06743ccb-b67e-4af2-a3b3-1a40a21217f5 (570.00) and, once declared, the recovery row.
  - deductibles withheld: 06743ccb-b67e-4af2-a3b3-1a40a21217f5 (120.00) only; a decision row is not a withholding.
Rows on the same traveller that are excluded and how: every row of the older certificate WLC2907145
(f79da3bc-e521-4cd7-910b-10c101041e25) — the claim rows d269a3fb-d00b-4769-821c-142f0764391e and c457d145-cadb-4431-8f4d-9d35f4919a09 and the premium rows 60ddb98f-9bca-40a6-a413-8cd6d4b9a976 and c1b68ceb-db2f-45cb-aeb9-4f0951e5574f —
is excluded because every aggregate in every compute of this task is scoped to the certificate
by care_policy_id, and that certificate is a different business object with its own 2024 journey.
No existing reversal, compensation or adjustment stands against BG-5520-26: the claims finder shows
the reference carries exactly two rows, the filing and the decision.

CHECK CARD 3 — PROBLEM-TREE CARD
  root: care_ext_settled_benefit_payment (settle_benefit_payment_411249ab, owner agent)
  edge root -> care_ext_supplier_recovery_declaration
     kind value_input; gate = the compute binding benefit_consumed; form state
     prerequisite sentence (verbatim from the root's own rule): "The benefit a settlement pays is
     fixed only after the benefit the certificate records as consumed carries a restoration for every
     amount a supplier has paid the traveller for a loss the certificate has already settled."
     four-point test: (1) ordering connective "only after"; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state
     — a restoration standing against the benefit consumed, named in the words the claims finder
     uses; (3) no tool, no policy id, no snake_case token, no row id; (4) strength "only after" and
     scope "every amount a supplier has paid ... for a loss the certificate has already settled",
     exactly the condition field and no wider.
     exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only
     declare_supplier_compensation_6de86425 writes a care_claim_recovery row, and it is the only
     policy in this file whose result is a restoration against the benefit consumed; the reader finds
     it from that policy's own rule ("that amount is restored to the benefit the certificate records
     as consumed") and from nothing else.
     derivation: the sentence says the settlement waits on a restoration standing against the benefit
     consumed; the claims finder shows the certificate carries a settled payment of 570.00 for the
     April delay and no recovery row at all; the air ledger shows the airline returned 600.00 on
     2026-08-14 against that same disruption; the only rule in the charter that produces a
     restoration is the supplier-compensation declaration, and that rule says the traveller declares
     it in their own name — so the agent must unlock that step and hand it to the customer.
     resolved_by declare_supplier_compensation_6de86425 (owner user)
     seed evidence it is false at the opening: initial_state.care_claims carries no row with
     event_type care_claim_recovery for b188f2e0-6e1b-4832-a156-c2862420bf5d, while initial_state.air_booking_events.19658f42-4f56-4be5-b53c-8f57c6eacba7
     .amount_usd = -600.00 with reason_code involuntary_schedule_change stands unanswered.
  edge root -> care_ext_outstanding_loading_charge
     kind state_gate; gate = care_premium_entries.charge_category; form state
     prerequisite sentence (verbatim from the root's own rule): "A settlement is paid on a
     certificate only after its premium lines carry every rating component the certificate's declared
     particulars call for."
     four-point test: (1) "only after"; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — which rating
     components the premium lines carry; (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) "only after" and "every
     rating component the certificate's declared particulars call for", exactly the condition.
     exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only
     charge_destination_loading_6e26c317 posts a destination loading line, and its policy is the only
     one in this file whose result is a destination loading line.
     derivation: the sentence says the settlement waits on the premium lines carrying every rating
     component the declared particulars call for; the certificate declares destination_region
     asia_pacific, and the premium finder shows lines of only three kinds — base_premium, age_loading
     and policy_fee — so the loading the declared region calls for is missing; the only rule that
     produces a destination loading line is the outstanding loading charge, and it is the desk's own
     action.
     resolved_by charge_destination_loading_6e26c317 (owner agent)
     seed evidence it is false at the opening: initial_state.care_premium_entries has exactly three
     rows for b188f2e0-6e1b-4832-a156-c2862420bf5d — de50d462-86c6-4369-816b-81c946e636c9.charge_category = base_premium, 6dc882c5-5eb7-41a0-b9c8-df6e4aea9c66.charge_category =
     age_loading and 02f9ab89-41c7-478e-acf8-886dcad67b0a.charge_category = policy_fee — and none of charge_category
     destination_loading.
  topological order: care_ext_outstanding_loading_charge, care_ext_supplier_recovery_declaration,
  care_ext_settled_benefit_payment. The two prerequisites are parallel; see order_uniqueness.
  per-edge deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run, figures below): skipping the recovery moves the scored
  settlement from 1410.00 to 900.00; skipping the loading leaves the certificate without the
  destination loading line, so the terminal state carries three premium lines instead of four.
  at least one problem is the customer's own write: declare_supplier_compensation_6de86425 is
  owner=user — declaring money a supplier paid YOU is the policyholder's own statement about their
  own affairs, the insurer cannot make it for them, and it completes on the spot.

STEP 1 — POLICIES (see care.extended.yaml)
FACTOR CARD — care_ext_outstanding_loading_charge (4 factors; scored amount_usd = 80.97)
 * protection_discount (parameter, cross_difficulty club). Ladder: active membership whose tier took
   effect on or before the issue date -> that tier's protection discount; active membership whose
   tier took effect after the issue date -> the house's standing discount (5); otherwise -> none (0).
   Tier taken here: the first. Evidence rows: club_memberships.fa9454dc-4746-4630-a3ed-1da4dd916202 (status active,
   tier_effective_date 2025-02-01 <= issued_date 2026-03-05, variant Wanderlane Platinum whose
   insurance_discount_pct is 10). Baseline reading: no discount at all; result then 89.96.
 * loading_base_basis (method). Ladder: a base premium line with re-rating adjustments -> the
   declared trip cost at the plan's base rate together with the adjustments; a base premium line and
   no adjustment -> the declared trip cost at the plan's base rate; otherwise -> the plan's minimum
   premium. Tier taken: the second. Evidence rows: care_premium_entries.de50d462-86c6-4369-816b-81c946e636c9 (base_premium
   578.34, so the certificate does carry a base premium line) and the absence of any
   premium_adjustment row. Baseline reading: the plan's minimum premium of 79.00; result then 9.95.
 * journey_exposure_share (parameter). Ladder: a journey longer than half the plan's longest single
   journey and a region other than domestic -> 100; a journey of half that length or less and a
   region other than domestic -> 70; otherwise -> 40. Tier taken: the second (19 days counted
   inclusively against TripGuard Plus's max_trip_length_days of 60). Evidence: care_policies.b188f2e0-6e1b-4832-a156-c2862420bf5d
   trip_start_date 2026-04-18, trip_end_date 2026-05-06, destination_region asia_pacific. Baseline
   reading: 40; result then 46.27.
 * purchase_lead_share (parameter). Ladder: cover bought less than a fortnight before the journey
   began -> 125; a fortnight or more but less than sixty days before it began -> 100; otherwise -> 75.
   Tier taken: the second. Evidence: care_policies.b188f2e0-6e1b-4832-a156-c2862420bf5d issued_date 2026-03-05 against
   trip_start_date 2026-04-18, which is 44 whole calendar days. Baseline reading: 75; result then
   60.73.
 Whole-baseline fall-back: 4.74. Near-miss planted: the older certificate f79da3bc-e521-4cd7-910b-10c101041e25 was issued on
   2024-08-01 against a journey beginning 2024-09-07, 37 days ahead, and its journey ran 15 days; a
   reader who aggregates the traveller's certificates rather than reading the one in hand lands on a
   different purchase-lead share and a different exposure share. It is excluded by the rule alone,
   which speaks throughout of "the certificate".
 No rule reads a stamp: there is no "loading applied" field anywhere in care_premium_entries, and the
   tier is established from the club record and the certificate's own dates.
FACTOR CARD — care_ext_supplier_recovery_declaration (4 factors; scored restored_amount_usd = -510.00)
 * supplier_return_scope (method, cross_difficulty air). Ladder: a disruption notice on the booking
   and the booking standing as travelled -> the amounts raised on that disruption alone; a disruption
   notice and the booking not standing as travelled -> the amounts returned in the six months to the
   declaration; otherwise -> every amount returned on the booking. Tier taken: the first. Evidence
   rows: air_bookings.5a0d3a52-6b1b-4534-97ea-dafe7354ad2f (status travelled), air_booking_events.a141127c-a077-461c-ba6b-25691eebe5e8 (the schedule change
   notice, 430 minutes, IRR-2291-JL) and air_booking_events.19658f42-4f56-4be5-b53c-8f57c6eacba7 (-600.00,
   involuntary_schedule_change). Baseline reading: every amount returned, which also sweeps in
   air_booking_events.d5712be9-96dc-45c8-9259-c2bd78f2a5d2 (-90.00, a routine bag refund); result then -586.50.
 * supporting_evidence_share (parameter, cross_difficulty air). Ladder: the supplier's return carries
   a notice reference and the settled claim names its evidence -> 100; a notice reference and no
   evidence named -> 90; otherwise -> 70. Tier taken: the first. Evidence rows:
   air_booking_events.19658f42-4f56-4be5-b53c-8f57c6eacba7 (notice_reference IRR-2291-JL) and care_claims.916dbbee-86d8-4394-814a-c2a141a1e8a7
   (supporting_document_reference DLY-88213). Baseline reading: 70; result then -357.00.
 * certificate_retained_share (parameter). Ladder: a deductible withheld from the settled payment and
   the supplier paying more than that payment -> 85; a deductible withheld and the supplier paying
   that payment or less -> 70; otherwise -> 100. Tier taken: the first (120.00 withheld, 600.00 paid
   against a 570.00 settlement). Evidence row: care_claims.06743ccb-b67e-4af2-a3b3-1a40a21217f5. Baseline reading: 100; result
   then -600.00.
 * restoration_bound_basis (method). Ladder: exactly one settled payment with a deductible withheld
   -> that payment together with the deductible; more than one settled payment with deductibles ->
   the total of the payments settled; otherwise -> the largest payment less the deductible withheld
   from it. Tier taken: the first (bound 690.00). Evidence row: care_claims.06743ccb-b67e-4af2-a3b3-1a40a21217f5, the only
   payout on the certificate. Baseline reading: 570.00 - 120.00 = 450.00; result then -450.00.
 Whole-baseline fall-back: -450.00. Near-miss planted: air_booking_events.d5712be9-96dc-45c8-9259-c2bd78f2a5d2 is a 90.00 bag
   refund that a careless reader adds to the airline's disruption money; the rule excludes it because
   the scope tier taken counts only what the airline raised on that disruption.
FACTOR CARD — care_ext_settled_benefit_payment (5 factors; scored paid_amount_usd = 1410.00)
 * benefit_limit_basis (method). Ladder: a per-traveller benefit and a loss suffered by one named
   traveller -> the plan's amount for that benefit; a share-of-trip-cost benefit and a declared trip
   cost -> that share of the declared cost; otherwise -> the plan's amount taken for each traveller
   named. Tier taken: the first (baggage_loss, insured_sequence 2). Evidence rows: care_claims
   .be63fa2e-bc8a-49d6-9b53-fd83571aa24f (claim_type baggage_loss, insured_sequence 2) and the plan's baggage_loss_limit_usd of
   1500.00. Baseline reading: 1500.00 x 2 travellers = 3000.00; result then 1590.00.
 * benefit_consumed_basis (method). Ladder: a settled payment and a restoration -> payments settled
   less amounts restored; a settled payment and no restoration -> the payments settled; otherwise ->
   the figure the benefit account carries. Tier taken: the first, once the restoration is declared
   (570.00 - 510.00 = 60.00). Evidence rows: care_claims.06743ccb-b67e-4af2-a3b3-1a40a21217f5 and the recovery row this task
   writes. Baseline reading: care_policies.b188f2e0-6e1b-4832-a156-c2862420bf5d.benefit_used_usd, which is 570.00 at the opening
   and stays 570.00 because no tool of this difficulty touches that account field; result then
   900.00.
 * supporting_document_share (parameter). Ladder: the allowed claim names its evidence and the
   evidence reached the insurer inside the plan's document deadline -> 100; named evidence arriving
   after the deadline -> 75; otherwise -> 50. Tier taken: the first (filed 2026-06-02, decided
   2026-06-18, 16 days against TripGuard Plus's claim_document_deadline_days of 60). Evidence rows:
   care_claims.c0b818e1-7bd4-4da8-87ff-36031d942c9d and be63fa2e-bc8a-49d6-9b53-fd83571aa24f. Baseline reading: 50; result then 780.00.
 * deductible_called_for_rate (parameter). Ladder: the emergency medical benefit with ceiling
   headroom left -> that benefit's own deductible; any other benefit with headroom left -> the plan's
   general per-claim deductible; otherwise -> nothing. Tier taken: the second (50.00, headroom
   150.00 - 120.00 = 30.00). Evidence row: care_claims.06743ccb-b67e-4af2-a3b3-1a40a21217f5.deductible_applied_usd = 120.00.
   Baseline reading: nothing; result then 1440.00.
 * deductible_ceiling_basis (method). Ladder: deductibles already withheld and less headroom than the
   deductible called for -> what remains of the ceiling; deductibles already withheld and headroom at
   or above it -> the deductible called for; otherwise -> the deductible called for taken for each
   traveller named. Tier taken: the first (headroom 30.00 < 50.00, so 30.00 is withheld). Evidence
   row: care_claims.06743ccb-b67e-4af2-a3b3-1a40a21217f5. Baseline reading: 50.00 x 2 = 100.00; result then 1340.00.
 Whole-baseline fall-back: 810.00. Near-miss planted: the certificate's own benefit_used_usd cache
   reads 570.00 and goes stale the moment the restoration lands, so an agent who reads the holding
   field instead of the ledger computes 900.00; the rule excludes it because the account figure is
   only the fall-through of the consumption ladder.
 Task-level floors: multi-source — every non-fall-through tier of supplier_return_scope,
 supporting_evidence_share, certificate_retained_share, restoration_bound_basis, protection_discount,
 loading_base_basis, benefit_limit_basis, benefit_consumed_basis, supporting_document_share,
 deductible_called_for_rate and deductible_ceiling_basis combines two conditions over distinct
 evidence; journey_exposure_share and purchase_lead_share each rest on a single date span, which is
 why the task's multi-source floor is met by the others. Cross-difficulty: protection_discount reads the club membership
 and its tier parameter; supplier_return_scope and supporting_evidence_share read the air booking and
 its ledger. Both categories are declared in cross_category and both are seeded for this traveller.

STEP 2 — TOOLS
capability contract cards:
 charge_destination_loading_6e26c317 — owner agent, rw write. User: the desk. Object: one travel
   protection certificate. Atomic action: post one premium line of the destination loading kind.
   Change: a new care_premium_entries row (event_type care_premium_charge, charge_category
   destination_loading, insured_sequence 0, currency USD, dated the day of posting, reason
   routine_issue). Observable: the line appears on the policyholder's premium statement. Receipt: one
   sentence carrying the new line reference, the certificate and the amount.
 declare_supplier_compensation_6de86425 — owner user, rw write. User: the policyholder in person.
   Object: the settled claim payment on their own certificate. Atomic action: record one recovery row
   restoring the declared money to the benefit consumed. Change: a new care_claims row (event_type
   care_claim_recovery, claim_status recovered, negative paid_amount_usd, source_claim_id = the
   payment it reverses, reason third_party_recovery). Observable: the certificate's claim record shows
   the recovery and that much benefit available again. Receipt: one sentence carrying the recovery
   reference, the certificate and the amount restored.
 settle_benefit_payment_411249ab — owner agent, rw write. User: the desk. Object: the insurer's
   decision row on one claim. Atomic action: record one payment settling it. Change: a new care_claims
   row (event_type care_claim_payout, claim_status paid, paid_amount_usd, deductible_applied_usd,
   source_claim_id = the decision, reason insurer_decision). Observable: the claim stands as paid on
   the claim statement. Receipt: one sentence carrying the payment reference, the certificate, the
   amount paid and the amount held back.
None of the three validates a prerequisite: each performs its CRUD with the arguments as given,
returns a normal receipt and raises nothing whatever the rest of the world looks like.

STEP 3 — SEED
Why each class of row exists, and what changes if it goes:
 - customers.4ca73258-c8d0-44c7-8655-2c91f04ce54b: the traveller; every finder and the identity check hang on it.
 - care_policies.b188f2e0-6e1b-4832-a156-c2862420bf5d: the certificate in hand; remove it and there is no computation at all. Its
   trip_cost_usd drives the rated base of the loading, its dates drive the exposure share, its
   destination_region drives the region share, its insured_count drives two ladder fall-throughs, its
   benefit_used_usd is the consumption fall-through, and its linked_air_booking_id is how the agent
   reaches the airline ledger.
 - care_policies.f79da3bc-e521-4cd7-910b-10c101041e25: a closed 2024 certificate. Distraction with a purpose — it proves the
   aggregates are scoped to one certificate; remove it and no scored value moves.
 - care_premium_entries de50d462-86c6-4369-816b-81c946e636c9 / 6dc882c5-5eb7-41a0-b9c8-df6e4aea9c66 / 02f9ab89-41c7-478e-acf8-886dcad67b0a: the three lines the certificate does carry.
   de50d462-86c6-4369-816b-81c946e636c9 puts loading_base_basis on its second tier, and the issue date of 2026-03-05 against a
   journey beginning 2026-04-18 puts purchase_lead_share on its second tier;; remove it and the loading falls to the
   minimum-premium tier and the scored amount becomes 9.95. Their absence of a destination_loading
   line is the falsified state of the second prerequisite edge.
 - care_premium_entries 60ddb98f-9bca-40a6-a413-8cd6d4b9a976 / a3d9c82a-b17a-4a79-8f6c-d7c9875406c3 / 3a3d52a2-46a7-4b5f-b91d-4c6ebb106937 / c1b68ceb-db2f-45cb-aeb9-4f0951e5574f: the old certificate's four
   rating lines, excluded by scope. Note in particular that the old certificate DOES carry a
   destination loading while the one in hand does not, which is exactly the contrast that makes the
   missing line visible to a reader who looks at both.
 - care_claims 916dbbee-86d8-4394-814a-c2a141a1e8a7 / 97886242-e3e2-487f-9b17-505edc9c2c9c / 06743ccb-b67e-4af2-a3b3-1a40a21217f5: the April delay claim, decided in part and settled.
   06743ccb-b67e-4af2-a3b3-1a40a21217f5 carries the 570.00 payment and the 120.00 deductible that three ladders read; remove it
   and the retained share, the restoration bound, the deductible headroom and the consumption all
   move.
 - care_claims c0b818e1-7bd4-4da8-87ff-36031d942c9d / be63fa2e-bc8a-49d6-9b53-fd83571aa24f: the lost-luggage claim and the allowance of 1620.00 the
   settlement pays against. Remove be63fa2e-bc8a-49d6-9b53-fd83571aa24f and there is nothing to settle.
 - care_claims d269a3fb-d00b-4769-821c-142f0764391e / c457d145-cadb-4431-8f4d-9d35f4919a09: a declined 2024 claim on the old certificate; scope distraction.
 - air_bookings.5a0d3a52-6b1b-4534-97ea-dafe7354ad2f and its six ledger rows: the journey the cover was bought with. a141127c-a077-461c-ba6b-25691eebe5e8 and
   19658f42-4f56-4be5-b53c-8f57c6eacba7 put the scope and evidence factors on their first tiers; d5712be9-96dc-45c8-9259-c2bd78f2a5d2 is the planted
   near-miss. Remove 19658f42-4f56-4be5-b53c-8f57c6eacba7 and the restoration is nothing and the settlement falls to 900.00.

user_scenario:
You are Sunniva Delacroix-Hale, fifty-eight, a structural engineer in Chicago who travels for work and takes one long holiday a year. You are unhurried on the telephone, a little dry, and you like being told what is actually happening rather than being reassured. In April you and your sister flew to Tokyo for a fortnight and the trip went badly: a long delay on the way out, and then her case never turned up at all. You claimed on the travel protection you bought with the flights. The delay claim was settled back in May and the money arrived. The lost-luggage claim you put in at the beginning of June, and in the middle of June you got a letter saying the insurer had allowed it. Nothing has ever been paid. That is the whole of why you are ringing: you want the lost-luggage claim actually paid out. You open by giving your name and the mobile number the bookings go to, 7732518064, and you say you are calling about a travel insurance claim that was approved in June and never paid.

You are happy for the desk to act for you on anything of its own, and you say so if you are asked. If the agent asks for more to confirm who you are, you give the last four characters of your passport, 1523, and if pressed further your date of birth, 30 September 1967, and the postal code on the card, 60622. You do not volunteer any of those unless asked. If you are asked for the claim reference you say you have the letter in front of you and read it out as BG-5520-26, and the certificate number as WLC3318472. You do not know what the insurer allowed, you do not know what any deductible is, and if you are asked what you think you are owed you say you have no idea, that is what you are ringing about. You cannot remember the exact figure on your sister's bag claim and say so rather than guess.

You have no idea how the premium on the certificate was put together and you have never looked at the individual lines. If the agent tells you that a rating line was missed when the certificate was written and has to go on now before anything can be paid, you take it calmly and tell them to do whatever the file needs; you do not argue about it and you do not ask what it comes to unless they offer. If the agent tells you that the airline has since paid you something for that April delay and that it has to go back against the cover before the luggage claim can be settled, you think for a moment and say yes, something did come back from the airline in the summer, you had forgotten about it; you agree to declare it yourself when the agent explains that it has to come from you. When the agent actually hands you that step to do, you do it, and afterwards you can repeat back whatever it tells you if the agent asks.

Only once the agent tells you that the luggage claim has been paid out do you wind the call up. You say that is a relief, thank them for sorting out something that had clearly been sitting there since June, and say goodbye. You do not ask for anything further, you do not ask for a letter or a statement, and you do not ask when the money will land. If the agent never mentions the premium line or the airline money you say nothing about either of them, because you would have no reason to know they mattered.
